subject: ela
intro: Good readers ask questions while they read, then find the answer right in the story. When you answer, point to the exact words that prove it. Ask WHO is in the story, WHAT happens, WHERE and WHEN it happens, WHY characters act, and HOW things happen. Referring to the text means you can show the sentence that gives the answer, instead of just guessing.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Rosa woke up early on Saturday. She tiptoed to the kitchen and mixed flour, sugar, and eggs in a big blue bowl. "These pancakes are for Mom's birthday," she whispered.

WHY did Rosa make pancakes?

steps: The question asks WHY, so look for a reason in the story.
Rosa says, "These pancakes are for Mom's birthday."
That sentence gives the reason directly.
solution.answer: Rosa made pancakes because it was her mom's birthday. The story says, "These pancakes are for Mom's birthday."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The old dog Biscuit followed Jamal to the bus stop every morning. He would sit by the bench until the bus came, then trot back home.

WHERE did Biscuit sit each morning?

steps: The question asks WHERE, so look for a place.
The story says Biscuit "would sit by the bench."
The bench is at the bus stop.
solution.answer: Biscuit sat by the bench at the bus stop. The story says he "would sit by the bench until the bus came."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the lights went out, Priya was not scared. She reached under her bed, pulled out a flashlight, and clicked it on. "I keep one right here for storms," she said.

HOW did Priya get light?

steps: The question asks HOW, so look for the action she took.
Priya "reached under her bed, pulled out a flashlight, and clicked it on."
Those steps show how she made light.
solution.answer: Priya got light by pulling a flashlight out from under her bed and clicking it on. The story says she "pulled out a flashlight, and clicked it on."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Every Friday, Grandpa and Leo walked to the pier to fish. They never caught much, but Leo loved watching the boats. "The fish can keep the water," Grandpa joked. "We came for the view."

WHAT did Leo love about the trips?

steps: The question asks WHAT Leo loved.
The story says "Leo loved watching the boats."
That is the detail that answers the question.
solution.answer: Leo loved watching the boats. The story says, "Leo loved watching the boats."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Maya's kite got stuck high in the oak tree. Her big brother Sam brought out a long rake and gently knocked it free. The kite floated down into Maya's arms.

WHO helped Maya get her kite down?

steps: The question asks WHO helped.
The story says "her big brother Sam brought out a long rake and gently knocked it free."
solution.answer: Sam, Maya's big brother, helped her get the kite down. The story says he "knocked it free" with a rake.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The class hamster, Nibbles, escaped during recess. The children found him an hour later, curled up asleep inside a rain boot by the door.

WHERE did the children find Nibbles?

steps: The question asks WHERE Nibbles was found.
The story says he was "curled up asleep inside a rain boot by the door."
solution.answer: They found Nibbles inside a rain boot by the door. The story says he was "curled up asleep inside a rain boot."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Deon practiced his speech in front of the mirror ten times. His hands still shook, but by the last try his voice was steady and clear.

WHY did Deon practice in front of the mirror?

steps: The question asks WHY he practiced.
He practiced so his speech would improve; by the last try "his voice was steady and clear."
The purpose was to get ready and calm down.
solution.answer: Deon practiced to get ready for his speech and calm his nerves. The story shows it worked: by the last try "his voice was steady and clear."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

A cold rain fell all afternoon, so the soccer game was moved to Sunday. The team spent Saturday inside, drawing plays on the whiteboard instead.

WHY was the game moved to Sunday?

steps: The question asks WHY the game moved.
The story says "A cold rain fell all afternoon."
The rain is the reason.
solution.answer: The game was moved because a cold rain fell all afternoon. The story names the rain as the cause.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the new student, Amir, could not find the library, Grace put down her lunch and walked him there herself. "I got lost my first week too," she said with a smile.

WHAT does Grace do to help Amir, and how do we know she is kind?

steps: The WHAT: Grace "put down her lunch and walked him there herself."
The HOW we know she is kind: she gives up her lunch time and says, "I got lost my first week too."
Point to both details.
solution.answer: Grace walks Amir to the library herself, even giving up her lunch time. We know she is kind because she stops eating to help and says, "I got lost my first week too."

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The power was out, so Nana lit two candles and taught the twins a card game she had played as a girl. By bedtime nobody even wanted the lights back on.

Ask one WHO question and one WHY question about this story, then answer each using the text.

steps: A WHO question: Who taught the twins a card game? Answer: Nana.
A WHY question: Why did Nana light candles? Answer: because the power was out.
Each answer points to a sentence in the story.
solution.answer: Sample WHO: 'Who taught the card game?' -> Nana. Sample WHY: 'Why light candles?' -> because "The power was out." Both answers come straight from the text.
